Level 2: Hardware

Cooling

Moves heat away from hot chips so they can keep running at full speed.

What is it?

The cooling system includes the CPU cooler (a metal heatsink with heat pipes and a fan), thermal paste between chip and cooler, and case fans that move air through the tower.

What does it do?

Heat flows from the chip into the cooler, spreads through heat pipes into thin metal fins, and fans blow air across the fins to carry the heat out of the case.

Why it matters

Chips slow themselves down (throttle) when they get too hot, around 95–105 °C for many CPUs. Good cooling keeps performance high and fans quiet.

Key specifications

Fan sizes
120 mm and 140 mm
Types
Air tower, liquid AIO, low-profile
CPU limit
often 95–105 °C before throttling

How it connects

  • CPURemoves its heat
  • GPUHas its own cooler
  • Power supplyHas its own fan

Fun fact

A heat pipe moves heat far better than a solid copper rod of the same size, because the liquid inside boils at the hot end and condenses at the cool end.
